# Agents

## What I mean by an agent

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A language model with tools. It reads files, writes code, runs it,
  and loops until a check passes
- Then it opens a pull request, a proposed change to the code that a
  person reviews before it is merged
- Not an RL policy. Not a chatbot
- I write the task and what counts as right. I read what comes back
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-agent.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A red box on the left, you, the task and what counts as right,
sends a prompt into a loop of four boxes: read the files and the docs,
write or change code, run it with tests lint and render, check passed.
No returns to the top of the loop. Yes leads to a red box on the right,
you, read the pull request, merge or send it back."}

::: {.attribution}
Diagram this talk, `scripts/keynote-schematics.py`
:::
:::
::::

## How I work now

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Most of the code I merge is agent-written. About half went in
  unreviewed
- Agents push from a bot account, a second GitHub login. Git shows
  who wrote what
- My time goes on writing the task and reading the result
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-bot-prs.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Bar chart of seabbs-bot pull requests opened per month in
2026: 17, 92, 78, 61, 124, 531, 744, 399, and 98 for September to the
11th shown in grey. Footer: 2,144 total, 85.5% merged, 11.9% closed
unmerged."}

::: {.attribution}
GitHub search API `total_count` per month, run 11 September 2026;
`seabbs-bot` created 23 January 2026 · review share: 712 of 1,371 merged
bot pull requests carried no review, counted for the
[how I LLM](https://samabbott.co.uk/how-I-llm) deck, August 2026
· `scripts/keynote-counts.py`
:::

## A live outbreak built this way

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- McCabe et al. published an outbreak size estimate on 18 May.
  A replication in a few hours the next day
- Refit on every push. 145 releases since 20 May
- The situation reports are French PDFs. Agents read them. Recent
  reports get two blind reads
- 333 of 425 pull requests by the bot. Four named authors
:::

## What was hard to check

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The onset curve exists only as a picture in the PDF. A digitiser
  reads counts off the pixels
- SitRep 081: JPEG compression left the axis ticks one pixel tall.
  The read came out 54% under the printed total
- SitRep 087: the y-axis grid moved from steps of 20 to 25. Caught
  only because counts on twelve-week-old dates fell
- Wrong answers look like right ones. Nothing crashes
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-onset-vintages.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Step lines of confirmed cases by week of symptom onset as read
from situation reports of 12 July, 26 July, 9 August, 23 August and
6 September 2026, rising from near zero in May to about 400 a week in
August, with the reads for the same week differing by up to a few tens
of cases between reports."}

::: {.attribution}
`data/README.md` in [BVDOutbreakSize][bvd-repo], SitRep 081 and 087
notes · figure from `data/onset_curve_scanned.csv`, read 11 September
2026, `scripts/keynote-onset-vintages.py`; each read sits a few percent
under the total printed on the figure
:::
:::
::::

## What changes

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Checking is now the slow step
- Components with their own checks give the agent something to test
  against
- Google's 2025/26 CDC hub entry was an LLM-guided tree search. It
  topped influenza, COVID-19 and RSV, prospectively
- Bracher and Funk put the earlier 11% retrospective gain down to
  data revision leakage
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-sai-loop.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Five boxes in a row, propose a forecasting model, write the
code, fit and forecast, score against held-out weeks, keep the best and
rewrite the rest, with a return arrow labelled a tree of candidate
models, many rounds."}

::: {.attribution}
Martinson, Brenner, Plomecka, Williams, Reich and Shamsi 2026,
[arXiv:2605.16238](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16238)
· Bracher and Funk 2026,
[arXiv:2608.05883](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.05883)
· team folders `Google_SAI-*` in the FluSight, COVID-19 and RSV hubs
· diagram this talk, `scripts/keynote-schematics.py`
:::
:::
::::

## What does not change

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Agents wrote the ingest, the fits, the tests and the release
  pipeline
- Choosing the model, reading the lower bound and judging
  ascertainment stayed with the authors
- "Who can do this work at all is narrowing. Agents make that worse"
- "I do not have a defence for this. I am part of the problem"
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-bvd-authorship.png){width="100%"

agent bot identities in teal, 50 from Dependabot in grey, 55 by hand in
